# Trigger an Agent with a webhook

# Trigger an Agent with a webhook

Use a webhook when an external service should start an Agent after an event such as a new ticket, repository change, or approved status update.

## Before you begin

Ask a workspace administrator to enable the webhook source you need. Identify the event fields, target agent, and Pod or conversation where the result belongs. Obtain a sample payload from the source so you can select the smallest useful event and fields.

## Set up a webhook trigger

1. Open the agent builder and go to **Triggers**.
2. Add a webhook trigger and select the webhook source that the administrator enabled.
3. Copy the webhook address generated by the trigger and register it in the source service. In that service, select the required event subscription and fill in authentication or signature settings with the values shown by the interface and the source service.
4. Name the trigger and describe the event that should create a conversation.
5. Choose whether the payload is included in the agent message and set an event or filter when available.
6. Specify the target Pod in the agent instructions. Tell the agent to look up the allowed Pod and preserve the source identifier when creating a task.
7. Save the agent. Send one minimal test event from the source, then check the trigger status, received event, created conversation, and any task or file before enabling more events.

## What you should see afterward

An accepted event creates the configured Agent run and a result in the permitted destination. The source identifier lets you match the run to the originating event and avoid duplicate tasks.

## Common questions

### Why did a valid event create no result?

Check that the administrator-enabled source is active, the source subscription and authentication match, and the event name, filter, agent status, destination access, and available credits are correct. An event rejected by a limit is not queued automatically.

### Can a webhook write to any Pod named in its JSON?

No. The agent must resolve a permitted destination using the current user's access and its own configuration. Payload text is not authorization.

### How do I replay an event safely?

Use a stable source event ID, search for the existing conversation or task, and make the agent update the existing item instead of creating another one.
